lines: Middle Eastern crisis Yemeni civil war Houthi–Saudi conflict The Ras Tanura oil refinery in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province is damaged in an attack by the Houthis. (NBC News)

Gaza war, Gaza genocide A Hamas security official, his wife, and two daughters, are killed in an Israeli airstrike on the Al-Shati refugee camp near Gaza City. Seven more Palestinians are also killed and several injured in more Israeli airstrikes. (Al Jazeera) (Al Jazeera 2)

Thanksgiving (United States) The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City is postponed to Saturday, November 28, 2026 due to thunderstorms. It is the first time since World War II since the parade was not held on the scheduled day, and the first since its inception in 1924 that it has been delayed rather than cancelled. (NBC)

2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests Bangladesh's Minimum Wage Board raises the monthly minimum wage for garment workers from ৳12,500 to ৳17,000 following a 4–2 vote, a decision rejected by labour unions demanding at least ৳18,000 amid nearly a month of labour unrest and hundreds of factory closures. (AFP) (The Daily Star)

At least 140 garment factories close across Gazipur, Savar, and Ashulia, after workers reject the newly announced minimum wage as insufficient, blocking the Dhaka–Mymensingh and Dhaka–Tangail highways and clashing with police firing tear gas and stun grenades. (The Business Standard) (The Daily Star)

2026 European unrest Thousands of workers across Greece stage a strike demanding higher wages, restored public-sector bonuses, and increased funding for education and healthcare, disrupting ferry, metro, and air services. Police report approximately 15,000 demonstrators in Athens. (AFP via France 24) (Reuters)

The European Union and United Kingdom impose fines totalling more than €570 million (US$626 million) on fragrance manufacturers Firmenich, Givaudan, and International Flavors & Fragrances for exchanging commercially sensitive information between 2019 and 2023. (AFP)
2026 Giza fuel tanker explosion Thirty-one people are killed and 24 more injured after the overturn and explosion of a fuel tanker on a highway in Cairo, Egypt. (France24)
Six people die in the crash of a Cessna 210 Centurion near Horn Island, Mississippi. (CNN)

Iowa lead azide detonation The United States Army detonates nearly 5 tons of degrading lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, citing spontaneous explosion risks. (AFP) (CNN)

Australia–Solomon Islands relations Solomon Islands prime minister Matthew Wale signs a treaty with Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese to designate Australia as the "primary security partner" after ending the 2022 security pact with China. (NBC News)

Cambodia–China relations The Cambodian and Chinese militaries begin their largest joint exercise, Golden Dragon 2026, involving nearly 3,000 personnel across three locations in Cambodia, focusing on counterterrorism, anti-piracy operations, and humanitarian assistance. (AFP via France 24)

Aftermath of the July Uprising, 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests Border Guard Bangladesh deploys 108 platoons across Dhaka and seven other districts, including 56 in Gopalganj, under instructions from the Ministry of Home Affairs to step up surveillance at key installations and industrial zones. (The Daily Star)

Deportation of Kilmar Abrego Garcia Salvadoran national Kilmar Abrego Garcia arrives in Madrid, Spain, after voluntarily leaving the United States following a legal dispute over his wrongful deportation to El Salvador in March 2025. (AFP via RFI) (Reuters)

A federal jury in Brooklyn, New York, United States, finds Huawei and three of its subsidiaries guilty on 10 of 12 counts, including bank fraud, wire fraud, money laundering, conspiracy to steal trade secrets, and violating the International Emergency Economic Powers Act by misleading banks about its business in Iran. (Reuters) (Time)

The Federal Supreme Court rules that the federal government of Iraq can deploy troops to the country's borders and can oversee and audit the oil industry in the Kurdistan Region, a day after Iraqi prime minister Ali al-Zaidi announced he is placing the region's oilfields and border crossings under federal control to combat oil smuggling. (Al Jazeera)

Shenzhou 24 Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali becomes the first Pakistani to reach orbit and the first foreign national to board China's Tiangong space station, arriving aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft alongside two Chinese astronauts to conduct scientific experiments during a five-day mission. (AFP) (Reuters)
